target.title: fix(auth): count token-type profiles in provider health status rollup
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After a user migrates from OAuth to a healthy token/setup-token credential, the gateway model-auth rollup can still report the provider as missing. This produces a false “model auth expired” warning even though the credential selected by runtime auth ordering is usable.

Fixes #97996.

## Why This Change Was Made

`buildAuthHealthSummary` already resolves the effective profile subset selected by explicit `auth.order`. The gateway projection was then looking only for OAuth credentials when an OAuth-capable provider was configured, so a selected token/setup-token profile disappeared from the provider status.

The final implementation fixes that projection boundary:

- Treat `effectiveProfiles`, including an empty array, as authoritative.
- Aggregate effective OAuth profiles first.
- If there is no effective OAuth profile, aggregate effective token/setup-token profiles.
- Keep a missing effective selection missing instead of falling back to unrelated inventory.
- Keep OAuth-configured API-key-only providers missing.
- Keep ordinary API-key-only providers on their existing static status.

The contributor’s two original commits remain in the PR history. The maintainer repair preserves SunnyShu’s credit while removing the proposed runtime fallback that would have weakened explicit `auth.order` precedence.

## User Impact

- Healthy setup-token migrations no longer appear expired or missing in model-auth status.
- Explicit auth-order exclusions remain enforced.
- OAuth remains higher priority than token credentials when both are effective.
- No configuration, migration, network, permission, or secret-handling behavior changes.

## Evidence

Prepared live head: `49039c25a513b20bd6a0e5acbdb50c96a1ba3d3a`

Captured main: `d18b843a478b0c32f0a5b6c16fa81879cea70df6`

The published head tree matches the reviewed local prepare lineage exactly. Relative to captured main, the candidate changes only:

- `src/agents/auth-health.test.ts`
- `src/gateway/server-methods/models-auth-status.ts`
- `src/gateway/server-methods/models-auth-status.test.ts`

Verification:

- Focused Vitest: 137 tests passed across the auth-health, gateway model-auth status, and CLI model-status suites.
- Blacksmith Testbox through Crabbox `tbx_01kweb9fjhshgtgv3gcp5jftxy`: exact candidate build passed.
- Same Testbox, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`: `openclaw models status --json` reported `claude-cli` as `ok` with the setup-token in `effectiveProfiles`.
- Same Testbox, running token-authenticated gateway: `models.authStatus` reported the provider and setup-token profile as `static`.
- Fresh Codex autoreview against captured main: no findings; patch correct, confidence 0.97.

Hosted exact-head checks completed with 76 passed and 13 skipped. Remaining failures are outside the captured-main patch: GitHub still evaluates the fork against frozen base `738b2be4b49b0182788e70abb5454faf82407a2d`, reporting hundreds of historical files. That causes dependency/label/path-scan failures plus lint, test-type, and Mistral-test failures in files unchanged from captured main. The repo-native prepare artifacts record the exact captured-main lineage and tree for the next serialized prepare step.

## Security Impact

- New permissions or capabilities: No
- Secret/token handling changed: No
- Network calls changed: No
- Command execution surface changed: No
- Data access scope changed: No

## Best-fix Verdict

Best bounded fix. The gateway projection owns this UI/status-specific OAuth-first policy. Changing runtime auth-order resolution would alter credential selection semantics, while suppressing the warning only in the UI would leave the gateway contract incorrect.

## AI Assistance

AI-assisted. Contributor credit and original commits are preserved.
